title: Grade 3 Science — Fri, Jun 20
description: Water — Day 5 of 5: Mixed review — water conservation and full week synthesis
subject: science

questions.question: Name two sources of freshwater:
questions.explanation: Freshwater sources include rivers, lakes, ponds, glaciers, groundwater (wells), and rain. Oceans are saltwater, not freshwater.

questions.question: The three states of water are:
questions.explanation: Water exists as solid (ice), liquid (water), and gas (water vapour). These are the three states of matter.

questions.question: Arrange the water cycle in order:
questions.explanation: Evaporation → Condensation (cloud) → Precipitation (rain/snow) → Collection (rivers/ground) → Evaporation again.

questions.question: Which is an example of WATER CONSERVATION?
options: Leaving the tap running while brushing teeth
Washing a car with a hosepipe for 30 minutes daily
Taking a quick shower instead of a long bath
Letting sprinklers water the garden in the afternoon sun
questions.explanation: A quick shower uses less water than a bath. Conservation means using water wisely and avoiding waste.

questions.question: Why should we NOT throw garbage into rivers?
options: Garbage pollutes water, killing aquatic life and making it unsafe to drink
It has no effect on water
Animals eat the garbage and are happy
questions.explanation: Water pollution destroys aquatic ecosystems, kills fish and plants, and makes water unsafe for humans and animals.

questions.question: What happens to most of the rain that falls in a forest?
options: Trees absorb some, soil holds some, plants transpire some, and some flows to rivers
It disappears into the ground and is lost
questions.explanation: In a forest, rain is absorbed by trees and soil, transpired back to the air, and slowly released to rivers. Forests are natural water regulators.

questions.question: Match: Evaporation → ___, Condensation → ___, Precipitation → ___
options: liquid to gas / gas to liquid / water falling from clouds
gas to liquid / liquid to gas / clouds forming
ice to liquid / liquid to gas / rain
questions.explanation: Evaporation = liquid → gas; Condensation = gas → liquid (clouds); Precipitation = water falling from clouds (rain/snow).

questions.question: Rainwater harvesting involves:
options: Collecting and storing rainwater for future use
questions.explanation: Rainwater harvesting collects rain from rooftops into tanks or allows it to seep into the ground to recharge groundwater.

questions.question: Which Indian city gets very little rainfall and relies on water from distant rivers?
questions.explanation: Chennai (in Tamil Nadu) often faces water shortages and relies on water from rivers like the Krishna. It has also implemented rainwater harvesting by law.

questions.question: Cutting down too many trees (deforestation) affects the water cycle because:
options: Fewer trees means less transpiration and less rainfall over that area
Trees have nothing to do with the water cycle
questions.explanation: Trees add moisture to the air through transpiration. Fewer trees → less moisture → less rainfall → dryer climate. Deforestation disrupts the water cycle.

questions.question: How does water vapour become rain?
options: Directly when it reaches the ground
Water vapour rises, cools, condenses into clouds, drops grow, then fall as rain
Wind pushes water vapour down as rain
Sun absorbs water vapour and spits it as rain
questions.explanation: Water vapour rises, cools at altitude, condenses into tiny droplets forming clouds. Droplets join and grow until heavy enough to fall as rain.

questions.question: Why should industries treat (clean) their waste water before releasing it into rivers?
options: Because dirty industrial water kills aquatic life and poisons drinking water
Because it is a government rule only with no real reason
questions.explanation: Industrial effluents contain harmful chemicals. Without treatment, they kill fish and plants and contaminate water that humans drink.

questions.question: Which saves more water: watering fields in the morning or at midday?
options: Morning (less evaporation — water reaches roots before sun is hot)
Evening is best and morning is worst
questions.explanation: Watering in the early morning reduces evaporation loss. At midday, the hot sun evaporates much of the water before it reaches plant roots.

questions.question: The water that you drank today may have been part of a dinosaur millions of years ago. Why is this possible?
options: The water cycle recycles the same water over and over across millions of years
Water is produced by the sun
questions.explanation: The water cycle has been recycling Earth's water for billions of years. The same water molecules cycle through evaporation, precipitation, and flow again and again.

questions.question: WEEK STAR: The best way to make sure future generations have enough water is:
options: Use as much as you want — there is plenty
Conserve water, prevent pollution, plant trees, and harvest rainwater
Send rockets to bring water from outer space
questions.explanation: Water conservation + preventing pollution + planting trees + rainwater harvesting together protect water for future generations. These are the pillars of water sustainability.
